title: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression
summary: A double-blind phase 2b trial at 38 sites in Australia, Europe and the US (Sept 2023–Apr 2025): 193 adults with moderate-to-severe depression unresponsive to 2–5 antidepressants (mean age 41; 59.1% female) received one intranasal dose with psychological support: 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73) or a 0.3 mg comparator (n = 74).
caveats: Industry-sponsored (several authors are affiliated with AtaiBeckley or Beckley Psytech; check the COI statement). Blinding a fast, intense psychedelic is hard even with an active low dose. The higher dose didn't beat the lower one, and follow-up is weeks, not long-term.

title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
summary: Using structure-guided 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin-biased agonists, the authors argue that β-arrestin signalling, not Gαq, drives prolonged antidepressant-like effects in mice. The key is kinetics: LSD dissociates slowly, so repeated low doses can accumulate receptor engagement close to a single high dose without the peak, sustaining β-arrestin signalling while limiting Gαq-mediated Ca²⁺ responses.
caveats: Animal behaviour stands in for both mood and subjective effects, and the absence of behavioural disruption doesn't mean the absence of altered experience. Funded by Chinese state and Shanghai sources (MOST, NSFC, CAS, ShanghaiTech). Several authors have filed patents on the new 5-HT2AR agonists through their universities (declared in the competing-interests statement), so the biased-agonist claims come from an interested party.

title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
summary: Baker, Kogan, Ma, Lu & Zuo. 5-HT2A signalling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was necessary and sufficient for psilocybin's synaptic remodelling but not for the head-twitch response: a cell-type route to the separation He et al. pursue via signalling.

title: Context Shapes Alpha-Band Electrophysiological Signatures under Psilocybin
summary: Described by the authors as the largest psilocybin EEG dataset to date (n = 56), with matched pre-drug baselines, recorded during movie viewing, eyes-closed rest, guided meditation and music. Source-space power, alpha peak frequency and coherence were analysed within and between seven networks across six bands (1–80 Hz), with FDR-corrected permutation tests and drug × context mixed models.
caveats: Preprint; effect sizes aren't in the abstract. Source-space coherence is still vulnerable to leakage (see Dimou, below); check dose and design in the full text.

title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
summary: van Hattem … Ziemann (Tübingen). With TMS to M1 (n = 29) or DLPFC (n = 11), a steeper pre-stimulus 1/f exponent predicted smaller early TEPs in both; alpha and beta power were inconsistent.

title: How well does EEG source imaging recover time series? Not very
summary: Dimou … Vulliemoz & Roehri (Geneva). Simultaneous high-density scalp and intracranial EEG in 34 patients: best reconstructed–recorded correlation 0.126, about 3 cm localisation error, heavy leakage.

title: Stimulus overlap confounds generalization in EEG foundation-model benchmarks
summary: Cui, Zhu, Xu & Huang. Across ten tasks from seven EEG emotion datasets, reusing stimuli across train and test inflated cross-participant accuracy every time (77% of above-chance performance on FACED-9).

title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface
summary: Shen … Claassen (Columbia). 13 of 41 (32%) unresponsive patients with acute brain injury achieved BCI control; consciousness recovered by discharge in 4/13 vs 1/28 without control (OR 21.2, 95% CI 2.3–930.7, very wide).

title: Artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation reveals phase-specific modulation of the human visual cortex
summary: Rhodes … Bono & Grossman. A front-end analogue low-pass filter (7th order, 90 Hz) keeps TI's difference-frequency artefact out of the EEG (22 participants; 4 recordings excluded).

title: Tuning in together: LSD enhances inter-brain synchrony and felt connectedness in romantic couples
summary: Mason, Czeszumski … (Maastricht). EEG hyperscanning of romantic couples (N = 25) on LSD 50 µg or placebo together: LSD raised felt connectedness, outlasting plasma levels, and increased inter-brain synchrony during shared rest.

title: Sex-related differences in outcomes following psilocybin or escitalopram: a Bayesian secondary analysis
summary: A post hoc Bayesian secondary analysis of the six-week double-blind psilocybin vs escitalopram RCT (N = 59, 20 female; psilocybin n = 30 with 11 female, escitalopram n = 29 with 9 female). There was no overall sex difference on any outcome, and none on the depression scales.
caveats: A secondary analysis of a trial that wasn't powered for sex effects, with 9–11 women per arm. Results are prior-sensitive, so treat them as hypothesis-generating.

title: Sex Differences in Acute Responses to Psychedelics: Evidence for Greater Subjective Intensity and Impairment in Female Participants
summary: Mason … Ramaekers. Pooled placebo-controlled data (94 drug observations, 51 female; psilocybin, 2C-B, LSD): women reported stronger effects on five measures (medium-to-large), with no difference in peak drug levels.

title: A scalable estimator of higher-order information in complex dynamical systems
summary: Liardi, Blackburne, Rajpal, Rosas & Mediano, Cell Reports Physical Science. 'M-information', via convex optimisation, scales with system size, is robust to noise, and indexes criticality, anaesthesia and task performance. A candidate for higher-order measures on many-channel EEG. doi:10.1016/j.xcrp.2026.103550 ·

title: Psychedelics restructure information in the human brain
summary: With Liardi, Mallaroni … Carhart-Harris, Timmermann, Muthukumaraswamy, Skipper & Mediano. Phi-ID across five psychedelics (N = 80) accounts for major prior results and is reproduced by a minimal model with reduced self-coupling: populations 'become alike, but not necessarily together'.

title: Psychedelics Restructure the Global Workspace of Consciousness
summary: Yousefi, Shinozuka … Luppi & Mediano. Across five drugs' fMRI, classic psychedelics added synergistic 'gateway' regions in frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks; MDMA and amphetamine reduced visual and somatomotor gateways.

title: Language-associated brain representations covary with disruption of selfhood under psilocybin
summary: Participants heard music and watched moving clouds in the scanner at baseline and after 19 mg psilocybin. The authors tested whether inter-subject similarity of brain activity increased with each pair's summed Ego Dissolution Inventory (EDI) score (N = 43), using elementary visual imagery (N = 49) and baseline as comparators.
caveats: Preprint. The brain–EDI correlation only just survives correction, and decoding with Neurosynth maps is a reverse inference.

title: Serotonergic psychedelics delay resting state neurovascular coupling dynamics
summary: Blind deconvolution of resting BOLD showed that both LSD and DMT increased estimated haemodynamic delays, in regions overlapping serotonin receptors involved in both psychedelic action and vascular regulation.
caveats: Preprint. Haemodynamic delay is estimated, not directly measured, and sample sizes aren't in the abstract.

title: Inferring brain structural complexity from dynamical measures
summary: They simulated Wilson–Cowan mean-field networks, rewiring connectivity step by step to grade the structural balance of integration and differentiation, and asked which complexity metrics track it.
caveats: A simulation study, so the conclusions hold only as far as the model class generalises. Preprint (v2 posted 26 Oct; numbers from the v1 full text).

title: Brain dynamics exhibit scale-dependent reversibility during consciousness transitions
summary: Rats under graded propofol were recorded with simultaneous local electrophysiology, whole-brain fMRI and pupillometry. LFPs, regional BOLD and pairwise FC changed largely reversibly between loss and recovery of consciousness.
caveats: Preprint, rodents, one anaesthetic; sample and effect sizes aren't in the abstract.

title: Brain state sets the spatial scale at which cortical geometry constrains human cortical dynamics
summary: Salinas-Medina … Liu & Evans (McGill). Histology-based neural field models suggest connectivity explains the broadest cortical patterns and geometry the finer ones, with brain state setting the scale.

title: Arousal-informed neuronal avalanches operate near criticality
summary: Stefens, Rajpal, … Barahona, Smith & Schultz. Two-photon imaging of thousands of neurons in awake mouse visual cortex (convNMF to separate avalanches) shows multiple subnetworks at different distances from criticality; arousal-linked avalanches sit nearest it, with the largest dynamic range.

title: A metric for comparing complex systems by their dynamics
summary: Ostrow … Fiete (MIT). Dynamical Similarity Analysis compares Koopman operators estimated from data; fast, robust to noise and partial observation.

title: Whole-brain normative modeling across multiple functional connectivity metrics in MEG
summary: Kobbersmed, Gohil, Woolrich & Vidaurre. M/EEG-FUNCOIN finds age and sex dimensions across several connectivity metrics in Cam-CAN MEG and flags individual deviations linked to cognition.

title: Effect of dulaglutide on functional and structural MRI changes during cigarette smoking cessation
summary: A predefined imaging substudy of an RCT (parent n = 255): 71 smokers were randomised to 1.5 mg dulaglutide (n = 35) or placebo (n = 36) for 12 weeks on top of varenicline and counselling, with structural and functional MRI at baseline and week 12 (59 completed).
caveats: An add-on design against strong standard care, so a ceiling effect is plausible. Modest sample size for a between-group imaging comparison.

title: The path from brain to words is rerouted in opioid addiction
summary: 82 people with opioid use disorder (OUD) and 34 controls watched the opening of Trainspotting in fMRI, then retold it; people with OUD showed a speech bias toward the drug scenes.
caveats: Preprint; imaging subsample of 65, cross-sectional, small control group, no test statistics in the abstract.

title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms
summary: A single-blind, sham-controlled pre–post study in people with elevated food-addiction symptoms, who did a food incentive-delay task with EEG during theta-band TI stimulation targeting a dACC-centred network.
caveats: Single-blind, N = 34, with key effects right at p ≈ .05, so preliminary. Numbers are from the preprint; the journal version is paywalled and I couldn't check whether they changed. 'Food addiction' is a symptom-scale definition, not a diagnosis. No competing interests declared. Full text paywalled; numbers from the preprint.

title: Altered brain-body activity during emotional mental imagery in major depressive disorder
summary: 37 controls and 35 patients with MDD did an emotional imagery paradigm with simultaneous EEG and ECG. Patients differed in alpha, gamma and delta activity (not ERPs), linked to worse cognition and symptoms, and HRV pointed to higher sympathetic activity.
caveats: Modest sample, cross-sectional, and coupling assessed by correlation rather than directional measures. Medication status isn't reported in the abstract.

title: Functional architecture of the human insula
summary: Quabs … Vogel & Parvizi. Intracranial stimulation and recordings in 87 patients define four regions (dorsal–posterior, ventral–posterior, mid-anterior, anterior–polar), with the anterior one driving the others.

title: Stress, Heartbeats, and Biases: Cardiac phase and acute stress modulate affective and spatial response bias.
summary: von Haugwitz … Larra (IfADo). In 31 participants, systole-timed targets and cold-pressor stress both strengthened emotional-prime effects on weapon/tool classification.

title: Multimodal autonomic arousal tracks dose-dependent affective dynamics during the acute effects of DMT
summary: D'Amelio … (Tagliazucchi group). Heart rate, electrodermal and respiratory signals in 19 people inhaling 20 or 40 mg DMT; a combined index tracked subjective emotional intensity.

title: Investigation of the pharmacological and circuit basis for psychedelic drug effects on interval timing in mice
summary: Male C57BL/6J mice judged whether a light lasted shorter or longer than 6.5 s. Psilocin (0.8 mg/kg SC) altered timing accuracy and precision; the 5-HT2A antagonist M100907 blocked this, the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100,635 didn't.
caveats: Male mice only, one psilocin dose, and a task far from human subjective time. No competing interests declared (NIDA funded).

title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
summary: Momi … Rembado. Neuropixels (46,360 units, 35 mice) plus scalp EEG: psilocybin reshaped burst firing; ketanserin abolished most effects.

title: Neurite Complexity and Plasticity Markers Track Synaptic Vesicle Density in the Living Human Brain: A Multimodal PET-MRI-EEG Study
summary: 18 healthy volunteers underwent [11C]-UCB-J PET (SV2A synaptic density), diffusion MRI with NODDI, resting-state fMRI and EEG plasticity tasks (roving mismatch negativity and visual LTP), before and after ketamine (n = 11) or DMT (n = 7).
caveats: Very small groups (11 and 7), so 'no significant change' isn't 'no change'. Healthy volunteers, one 1–8 day window. Preprint.

title: Substantial Treatment-Seeking Interest, Narrow Eligibility: Diagnostic Heterogeneity and External Validity in the PRIDE Psilocybin Trial—Relevance to Precision Psychiatry
summary: Inserra … Martinotti, Behavioral Sciences. At PRIDE's coordinating site (phase II, psilocybin vs personalised neuromodulation for TRD), 54 of 67 screened candidates (80.6%) were excluded and 8 treated, mainly for not meeting protocol TRD or another diagnosis (50%), age (18.5%), suicidal ideation (13%) and SUD (9.3%).

title: Multimodal Machine Learning–Based Prediction of Relapse in Major Depressive Disorder
summary: Teutenberg … Kircher, 21 Oct. In 564 patients (270 relapsed), balanced accuracy was 47.2–64.4%; the best model used a few clinical risk factors, and adding modalities didn't help.

title: What drives apparent dynamic functional connectivity in resting-state fMRI?
summary: Griffin … Vidaurre & Woolrich (Oxford). On HCP resting fMRI, HMM states varying in mean and variance explained most apparent dynamics, with little gain from state-varying FC or for behaviour prediction.

title: Most-read neuro preprints, October 2026 to date (biorxiv-top)
summary: #1 is Aizenbud's 'What can a neuron compute'. Picks for you: surface electrophysiology toward a whole-brain interface (Ho, #3), Ostrow (#7, above), global brain dynamics (Kochalka, #12), Momi (#33), Mason on LSD (#72, EEG), psilocybin and visual change detection (De Filippo, #98), D'Amelio on DMT (#124).
caveats: Ho, Kochalka and Aizenbud verified by title and rank only.

title: pybemobil, first public release
summary: Python/MNE port of the BeMoBIL mobile brain/body pipeline: XDF loading, ECG/EMG/EDA alignment, EEG preprocessing (ZapLine-plus, ASR, ICLabel), BIDS export.

title: Open data from the food-addiction EEG study
summary: Wen et al.'s de-identified behavioural and ERP data; scripts promised on publication.

title: ICYMI: mne-denoise 0.0.3
summary: An EEG/MEG denoising toolbox including DSS, ASR, ZapLine and SSP-SIR for TMS-EEG artefacts.

title: ICYMI: MNE-ICALabel v0.10.0
summary: Automatic labelling of ICA components for EEG, MEG and iEEG in MNE-Python.

title: ICER will assess COMP360 psilocybin for TRD
summary: Comparators: esketamine/IV ketamine and rTMS. Draft-scope comments due 5 pm ET, 10 Nov (publiccomments@icer.org); CEPAC meeting 20 May 2027.

title: FDA request for information on ibogaine trials
summary: FDA wants input on early ibogaine trial design and safety, including a starting dose of no more than 10 mg/kg; HHS is funding trials in OUD and PTSD. Docket FDA-2026-N-10429.

title: Stakeholder responses to FDA's psychedelics docket
summary: Psychedelic Alpha's analysis of comments to FDA's psychedelics Part 15 docket (closed 5 Oct): mostly supportive, somewhat divided.

title: Why pharma firms are betting billions on psychedelic drugs despite setbacks
summary: 'Why pharma firms are betting billions on psychedelic drugs despite setbacks' (title only verified).
caveats: Verified by title only.

title: New on ClinicalTrials.gov: psilocybin for depression in veterans (first posted 26 Oct)
summary: NCT07895134 (VA ORD). Phase 2, 150 planned, start Jan 2027: one psilocybin dose plus brief ACT, with arms adding modafinil, zolpidem and/or pimavanserin.

title: OHBM 2027, Toronto, 26–30 June 2027
summary: Abstracts open 2 Nov, close 14 Dec 2026 (650 words, up to 2 figures, $45).

title: Breaking Convention 2027, University of Exeter, 15–17 April 2027
summary: Dates confirmed on Breaking Convention's Substack; no 2027 call for participation yet.
caveats: Call for papers not yet published.

title: Psychedelic Science 2027 (MAPS), Denver, 3–7 May 2027
summary: Early-bird registration is open, with adult registration from $799.

title: ECNP Congress 2027, Barcelona, 25–28 Sept 2027
summary: 40th ECNP Congress, CCIB Barcelona. Abstract and registration dates aren't published yet.
caveats: 2027 dates and deadlines not yet published.

title: Neuromatch Computational Neuroscience, online, 5–23 July 2027
summary: Applications 10 Feb–17 Mar 2027.

title: CAJAL NeuroAI, Champalimaud, Lisbon, 5–23 July 2027
summary: Course fee €3,500. Applications open in 2027.

title: MBL Methods in Computational Neuroscience, Woods Hole, 24 July–21 Aug 2027
summary: Applications due 10 Mar 2027. Directors Stefano Fusi (Columbia) and Roozbeh Kiani (NYU); financial aid available.

title: NOW · Guarantors of Brain travel grants (UK)
summary: UK PhD students presenting original work: up to £500 (UK), £800 (Europe), £1,200 (elsewhere), co-funding expected. Rolling; submit ≥8 weeks before the meeting.

title: PLAN · Wellcome Early-Career Awards (UK)
summary: Salary plus up to £400k expenses over about 5 years; no fixed deadlines (interviews May and Sept 2027). Needs a completed PhD, normally ≤3 years postdoc, and from 29 Oct 2026 a UK or eligible LMIC base.

title: PLAN · Leverhulme Early Career Fellowships (UK)
summary: Closes 4 pm, 18 Feb 2027. Your thesis must be submitted for viva by the deadline and no more than 4 years before it, so the 2028 round is the realistic target.

title: PLAN · MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (EU, any nationality)
summary: 2027 call planned to open 7 Apr 2027, deadline 8 Sep 2027 (may change). Needs a PhD by the deadline, ≤8 years' research experience and ≤12 months in the host country in the previous 36.
caveats: Call dates are planned dates and may change.

title: PLAN · NIH K99/R00 Pathway to Independence (US)
summary: For mentored postdocs, generally ≤4 years of postdoc experience; non-US citizens eligible. Deadlines 12 Feb, 12 Jun and 12 Oct.

title: WATCH · NHMRC Investigator Grants, EL1 (Australia)
summary: 2027 round closed 29 Jul 2026; EL1 is typically 0–5 years post-PhD. Per the 2027 guidelines (s4.1.1), the lead must be an Australian/NZ citizen, permanent resident or hold a suitable work visa, and spend ≥50% of the grant, including the final year, in Australia.
caveats: Rules read from a third-party PDF copy of the guidelines.

title: Toward A Whole-Brain Interface Enabled by High-Resolution Surface Electrophysiology
summary: #3 most-read neuro preprint in October 2026 on biorxiv-top.
caveats: Listed by title and rank only. Ho, Kochalka and Aizenbud verified by title and rank only.

title: Causal and directional elements of global brain dynamics
summary: #12 most-read neuro preprint in October 2026 on biorxiv-top.
caveats: Listed by title and rank only.

title: Psilocybin collapses visual change detection and drives cortical dynamics toward a state of surprise
summary: #98 most-read neuro preprint in October 2026 on biorxiv-top.

title: Quiet breathing evokes scalp EEG potentials in wakefulness and in every sleep stage
summary: Using Cleveland Family Study polysomnography from 729 participants (median 7,871 respiratory cycles each), the authors averaged EEG time-locked to inspiration onset. They found a pre-inspiratory component about 300 ms before inspiration and post-inspiratory peaks up to 3 s after. The potentials persisted in N2, N3 and REM sleep with a simplified, K-complex-like shape, alongside more spindle-range activity. They were present regardless of BMI and unchanged in the 203 participants without sleep-disordered breathing.
caveats: What these potentials mean physiologically or clinically is still unknown, and scalp EEG can't say where they come from. Polysomnography montages are sparse.

title: A canonical microcircuit DCM for estimating excitation/inhibition balance from ERPs
summary: Requested by you, so it's outside the usual one-week window. The authors extend the convolution-based canonical microcircuit (four populations: spiny stellate, superficial pyramidal, inhibitory interneurons, deep pyramidal) with two global (across-region) excitability parameters, modelled as self-inhibition: one for pyramidal (E) cells and one for inhibitory (I) cells, plus condition-specific modulations of each. They fitted healthy EEG from B-SNIP and NAPLS-2 in three paradigms, each with a six-region network: paired clicks (n = 266), a passive double-deviant MMN oddball (n = 241) and an acti
caveats: The patient-like effects are simulations; no patient data were fitted. I-cell recovery is only fair and test–retest reliability is unknown. The E self-inhibition parameter might partly reflect a PV interneuron loop rather than pyramidal cells themselves. Code and empirical priors are public (SPM12 r7771, MATLAB). No competing interests declared; funded by Adams's UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship and Wellcome (Friston). Version of record 27 Oct.

title: Travelling waves may hold working memory without overwriting it
summary: In an artificial neural network simulation, transient travelling waves produced minimal synaptic plasticity, letting working memory be updated without interference. In human intracranial recordings from the temporal lobe, waves started at encoding and persisted through maintenance and recall; on error trials there was no continuous wave activity.
caveats: Preprint; intracranial coverage is clinically determined, and sample sizes and effect sizes need checking in the full text.

title: LSD in simultaneous PET-MRI: high 5-HT2A occupancy, more cerebral blood flow, less global connectivity
summary: Healthy volunteers, blinded to dose, had simultaneous PET-MRI after LSD. LSD occupied 5-HT2A receptors with high affinity, increased global cerebral blood flow and internal carotid flow, and decreased global functional connectivity; the connectivity decrease was negatively associated with the CBF change. Subjective effects showed anticlockwise hysteresis against plasma levels. A separate psilocybin cohort (n = 25) showed the opposite pattern: lower CBF and higher global FC.
caveats: Small sample for the LSD PET arm. The opposite LSD/psilocybin haemodynamic patterns complicate comparing BOLD effects across drugs.

title: PhaseICA: ICA that keeps phase, to extract propagating 'brain waves' (preprint v2, 26 Oct).
summary: Ma, Li, Adali, Iraji, Fu & Calhoun. Complex-valued ICA on Hilbert-transformed signals recovers recurring spatiotemporal propagation patterns that amplitude-only ICA discards. Potentially useful for the spatial structure of your fMRI psychedelic data.

title: A brain–heart–gut network that lives mostly at infra-slow timescales
summary: Using open-access simultaneous resting EEG, ECG and EGG from 28 healthy participants, the authors related brain alpha power, cardiac sympathetic and parasympathetic indices and gastric rhythm power using the maximal information coefficient across time delays, with surrogate testing. Interactions formed a multidirectional brain–heart–gut network, mainly at infra-slow timescales (0.01–0.1 Hz).
caveats: Small sample at rest only; MIC detects dependence, not causation.

title: Temporal interference in mouse cortex: the kilohertz carrier alone activates neurons, and the envelope organises rhythm
summary: Two-photon imaging in mice, immunohistochemistry and modelling showed that kilohertz stimulation without amplitude modulation evoked widespread activity. The amplitude modulation organised rhythmic responses at the modulation frequency, strongest near the interference centre.
caveats: Preprint in mice; field strengths and geometry that may not translate to human scalp TI.

title: Conscious and suppressed images alternate about 15 times a second in the primate brain
summary: Neuropixels recordings from macaque IT face patches and prefrontal cortex during binocular flash suppression (validated behaviourally in 14 humans) showed activity alternating about 15 times a second between micro-epochs representing the conscious and the suppressed image; either could be reconstructed depending on the epoch, and feature tuning was amplified in conscious epochs.
caveats: Preprint, macaques; the link between micro-epochs and reported experience is inferred.

title: New on ClinicalTrials.gov: ayahuasca and cerebral metabolism, a PET study (first posted 26 Oct).
summary: NCT07893912 (University of São Paulo). Early phase 1, 15 participants planned.

title: Also new: ayahuasca dose and personality (first posted 26 Oct).
summary: NCT07893769 (University of São Paulo). Early phase 1, 28 enrolled (actual).

title: SfN Neuroscience 2026, Washington DC, 14–18 Nov 2026.
summary: In two weeks.

title: Psilocybin for alcohol use disorder: a short-term signal that mostly fades
summary: Six trials (N = 202; three RCTs). Short term, psilocybin reduced drinks per day (SMD 0.48, p = 0.004), % drinking days (0.50, p = 0.009) and % heavy drinking days (0.39, p = 0.020). At 4–28 weeks only % drinking days held (SMD 0.41, p = 0.032). Abstinence odds were higher (OR 2.78, p = 0.029). Adverse events were mostly mild.
caveats: Few, small, heterogeneous trials, including open-label ones; the authors call the evidence mixed.

title: Fitting a corticothalamic neural field model to each patient's EEG separates minimally conscious from unresponsive states
summary: A biophysically informed corticothalamic neural field model was fitted to high-density EEG from two large independent datasets: 203 patients with unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS), 270 in a minimally conscious state (MCS) and 74 healthy controls. The fitted model captured spectral features across states of consciousness and showed reduced corticothalamic integrity in patients, more so in UWS than MCS, consistent with the mesocircuit hypothesis. EEG simulated per subject reproduced the empirical complexity patterns, and permutation entropy distinguished MCS from UWS in both real and simul
caveats: Spectral fitting constrains corticothalamic parameters only indirectly, and classification performance needs checking in the full text. It drew attention on Hacker News (73 points), which is unusual for a modelling paper.

title: 'Cortical excitability' isn't one thing: six distinct dimensions in resting and 40 Hz MEG
summary: In a large sample of healthy adults with whole-head MEG at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation, the authors compared stimulus-driven synchronisation, spectral power, aperiodic (1/f) activity, signal complexity, long-range temporal correlations and phase–gamma synchronisation. Hierarchical clustering found six distinct excitability dimensions with little redundancy. Aperiodic and alpha measures were strongly coupled and best aligned spatially with stimulus responses; temporal, complexity and synchronisation measures were largely independent. Each dimension related differently to cortical
caveats: Healthy adults only; sample size and the receptor-map method need checking in the full text, and receptor associations are spatial correlations across regions, not within people.

title: Weaker forward theta travelling waves at rest in OCD
summary: Resting (eyes closed) and task EEG (Go/NoGo, Flanker) in 25 people with OCD and 27 controls. Forward (posterior-to-anterior) and backward waves along midline electrodes were quantified with 2D FFTs in theta and alpha. At rest there was a group × direction interaction in theta (P = 0.0006): weaker forward waves in OCD. During the Flanker task, forward theta increased more from rest in OCD (P = 0.022). There were no alpha or backward-wave differences and no links to symptom severity.
caveats: Small groups, midline electrodes only, and no symptom association.

title: EEG generators: what the skull does to cortical signals, measured directly (mice, 27 Oct).
summary: Mo … Song, Biosensors and Bioelectronics. Micro-ECoG and skull-screw EEG on one clock in awake mice (115 pairs, 3 mice): cortex-to-skull gain rose with frequency following a power law (skull EEG relatively preserves high frequencies) and shifted across task blocks. A calibration target for forward models and for interpreting aperiodic slopes. Tiny n.

title: A single psilocybin dose in macaques: network reorganisation, an anti-inflammatory CSF shift and raised prefrontal glutamate for a week
summary: Multimodal MRI, MRS, CSF proteomics and metabolomics, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing in cynomolgus macaques. Psilocybin increased frontoparietal integration with default-mode and limbic networks, transiently reduced its integration with somatomotor network and induced global segregation; some cortical, striatal and thalamic changes lasted a week. CSF shifted from acute prostaglandin-dominated inflammation to a sustained omega-3-associated anti-inflammatory state, with sustained rises in dlPFC glutamate/glutamine and total creatine.
caveats: Preprint; animal numbers and dose need checking, and many modalities raise multiple-comparison questions.

title: Low-dose ketamine raises BOLD entropy in treatment-resistant depression (J Affect Disord, 26 Oct).
summary: Liou … Chen. Two RCTs: sample entropy rose by day 3 in gyrus rectus, cerebellar vermis, substantia nigra, red nucleus and locus coeruleus (Trial 1) and in left amygdala (Trial 2, vs midazolam). A neuromodulatory-hub angle on entropy accounts.

title: The same E/I input shift gives different aperiodic slopes depending on circuit wiring
summary: The authors embedded electron-microscopy-reconstructed cortical microcircuits in near-critical dynamics and generated field potentials with fixed synaptic, membrane and forward-model parameters. The relationship between E/I input and the aperiodic exponent differed between biological and topology-randomised networks (a significant E/I × topology interaction). In paired cortical ECoG and thalamic recordings from juvenile pigs under propofol, exponent changes were larger in thalamus than cortex, even after accounting for global state, baseline spectra and distance from criticality.
caveats: A model-plus-animal study; the pig recordings are under anaesthesia, and the claim is about interpretation, not a new estimator.

title: DCM parameters sit between spectra and clinical scores for classifying individuals
summary: Resting MEG from 74 controls, 45 people with behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia and 55 with progressive supranuclear palsy. Clinical scores classified individuals well (controls vs PSP accuracy 0.94), MEG spectral features weakly (~0.6) despite clear group differences, and DCM-inferred biophysical parameters in between (PSP vs controls 0.70; bvFTD vs PSP 0.74) while staying mechanistically interpretable.
caveats: Preprint; classification is used as an exploratory probe, and neurodegeneration is far from your populations.

title: Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement changes prefrontal drug-cue responses in opioid use disorder
summary: An RCT in inpatients with OUD: 8 weekly MORE sessions vs supportive therapy. In the cue-reactivity task (n = 59), MORE reduced drug-biased activity in middle frontal gyrus and precuneus when downregulating drug-cue responses relative to upregulating natural-reward responses. MORE also reduced medial PFC synchronisation to drug scenes in a movie (n = 37) and extended abstinence at about 4 months (χ² = 6.7, P = .04; Cohen w = 0.19).
caveats: Imaging subsets are small and unequal (24 vs 35), and the abstinence effect is modest.

title: Psilocybin, cognitive stability and drinking in AUD with depression (medRxiv, 29 Oct).
summary: Sayalı … Barrett. Secondary analysis of an RCT (12 psilocybin, 13 placebo): psilocybin slowed cued task switching, but most of 34 cognitive measures were inconclusive and none survived FDR. Drinking fell in both arms, and shifts toward stability tracked drinking reduction. Small and exploratory.

title: MDMA-assisted therapy for veterans with PTSD and alcohol use disorder (Alcohol, 30 Oct).
summary: Eaton … Haass-Koffler. First open-label pilot (N = 10): PTSD symptoms fell (d = 1.24); drinks per drinking day fell 31% and heavy drinking days 54%, not clinically significant; no serious adverse events.

title: Brain–body timing during emotional videos (MEG + physiology preprint, 29 Oct).
summary: Xu … Parviainen. 92 participants, MEG plus cardiac, electrodermal, respiratory and facial EMG. Corrugator activity preceded matching neural patterns by about 1 s, while heart rate and electrodermal activity followed by about 1.7 s and 4.5 s; respiration rate didn't exceed the decoupled reference.

title: Psilocybin tilts learning toward rewarded outcomes in rat prefrontal cortex
summary: In a value-based probabilistic choice task with computational modelling and mPFC single-unit recordings, psilocybin improved choice under uncertainty and shifted learning rates bidirectionally: more updating from rewarded actions, less from unrewarded ones. Neural encoding of rewarded outcomes strengthened and of unrewarded outcomes weakened.
caveats: Rodents; acute exposure; an eLife reviewed preprint with public reviews, not a final version of record.

title: ASCENT: an EEGLAB plugin for entropy, fractal and aperiodic measures (PsyArXiv, 27 Oct).
summary: Cannard & Delorme. Single-scale, multiscale and multivariate entropy, fractal dimension and aperiodic parameterisation on channels or ICs, with time-resolved multiscale entropy and aperiodic estimates, GUI and command line.

title: LSD for depressive symptoms: a meta-analysis of five RCTs
summary: Five RCTs (N = 227), preregistered: LSD reduced depressive symptoms vs comparators (adjusted SMD −0.65, 95% CI −0.92 to −0.38), with no significant heterogeneity and three studies at low risk of bias. Severe adverse events possibly related to study parameters included three hospitalisations.
caveats: Depression was mostly a secondary outcome in anxiety trials, and designs varied (three with psychological support).

title: Psychedelics and psychosis, 1984–2025: a systematic review (J Psychopharmacol, 27 Oct).
summary: Silva Reis … Dos Santos. 52 papers: no consistent population-level link; one transient case in controlled trials; risk factors are personal or family history and unsupervised use.

title: Psychedelics for addiction: treatment or a 'learning window'? (Brain Sciences, 29 Oct).
summary: Buciuc, Gold & Fuehrlein. Compound-by-compound review; the strongest human signals are psilocybin in tobacco and alcohol use disorders, though the alcohol signal rests on two small, discordant RCTs.

title: Psilocybin's rapid antidepressant effect came without a group-level rise in SV2A, but baseline SV2A predicted who improved
summary: A pre-registered [11C]UCB-J PET sub-study of a published randomised trial. Thirty-five people with moderate-to-severe recurrent major depression were randomised 1:1 to a single 25 mg psilocybin dose or 100 mg niacin as active placebo, both with psychotherapeutic support. PET ran 2–7 days before and 15 (±7) days after dosing, quantifying SV2A (a synaptic vesicle protein used as a proxy for synaptic density) in hippocampus and frontal cortex. Despite significant clinical improvement in the psilocybin group, there was no evidence of a group-level SV2A increase relative to niacin (VT or BPND). In secondary analyses, higher baseline VT went with greater later improvement after psilocybin, survivi
caveats: Preprint. Small PET sample (n = 35 across two arms). SV2A is an indirect marker of synaptic density, and PET resolution can't see local or cell-type-specific remodelling; the scan was about two weeks after dosing, so a transient change earlier on can't be ruled out. The baseline-predicts-response finding is secondary and needs replication.

title: Read it alongside (ICYMI, Translational Psychiatry, 15 Jul; covered by PsyPost 3 Nov):
summary: Johansen, … Knudsen (Copenhagen) gave 15 healthy volunteers 0.3 mg/kg psilocybin with [11C]UCB-J PET at baseline and one week. The open-label, single-arm study stopped for futility at interim (mean change about 2–3%, not significant). Exploratory: people dosed in a therapy-like room rather than an MRI scanner had more intense mystical-type experiences and larger SV2A increases, but setting wasn't randomised (the first five were scanned). Two independent groups, the same tracer, no robust group-level effect.

title: Attention travels as a wave at the rhythm of whichever sense is cueing it
summary: Alpha lateralisation is a standard marker of sustained visuospatial attention, and anterior-to-posterior alpha travelling waves had recently been shown to lateralise too. The question here: are the waves top-down attention signals or a by-product of attending to visual input? The authors cued attention through different senses (auditory cueing vs visual stimulation) while keeping a visual discrimination task. With auditory cueing, lateralised travelling waves appeared in theta; with visual stimulation, in alpha. Wave lateralisation at both frequencies correlated trial by trial with alpha power lateralisation, which the authors read as attention signals propagating at the intrinsic rhythm of
caveats: Preprint; sample size and wave-detection details need checking in the full text. Scalp travelling-wave estimates are sensitive to volume conduction and reference choice.

title: How often can you actually see an MMN in one person? A benchmark in healthy controls and minimally conscious patients
summary: 48 healthy controls and 26 patients in a minimally conscious state (MCS) completed six auditory paradigms: multifeature MMN, passive and active oddball P300, own-name, semantic oddball and sentence N400. Effects were classified with blinded expert visual scoring, ROI ANOVA, cluster-based permutation and SVM decoding. In controls, visual scoring found an MMN to at least one deviant and a P300 in both oddball tasks in all 48; task-related P300 enhancement (command following) was detected in 81%, sentence-congruity effects in 69% and the own-name effect in only 35%. Patients showed lower detection: MMN in 27% for the short-duration deviant and 65% when any of five deviant types counted. Prognos
caveats: Preprint; modest patient sample, and detection rates depend on which classification method you choose.

title: Walking flattens the aperiodic exponent and delays the auditory N1 (preprint, 6 Nov).
summary: Chen, Chen, Zhang & Cao (Zhejiang). Mobile EEG in 30 adults: walking delayed N1 latency (< 10 ms), with a scalp-wide decrease in aperiodic exponent, and larger exponent drops went with larger N1 delays. A reminder that state (posture, movement) shifts the exponent you might read as E/I.

title: Aperiodic exponent as a stimulation-response predictor (NeuroImage, 2 Nov).
summary: van Bueren, … Cohen Kadosh. tRNS sped learning vs sham without reliably shifting resting exponent or fNIRS HbO; higher resting exponent and lower resting HbO went with larger gains, but the EEG moderation effects weakened with participant-specific slopes, and the authors call for replication. Relevant background for predicting TI responses from baseline EEG.

title: Most-read neuro preprint pick (#21 in October on the bioRxiv tracker): sustained attention, alpha and the 1/f slope.
summary: Barne, Fu & Lavie (UCL). EEG during a continuous performance task under low vs high perceptual load: time-on-task increased alpha power widely and steepened the 1/f slope in a left temporoparietal cluster, alongside worse detection and more mind wandering. A tidy within-session example of periodic and aperiodic changes moving together. (The October #1, the rapid-alternation consciousness preprint, was in #002.)

title: Oscillations and the aperiodic exponent are coupled only sometimes, and local inhibition decides when
summary: Bias-reduced analyses of 3,245 intracranial contacts from 61 awake people found significant coupling between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent in fewer than 13% of contacts per band. A connectome-constrained dynamical model predicted that neither changing input to a local circuit nor removing long-range connections would modulate the coupling, whereas stronger local inhibitory feedback would make frequency and exponent covary. Three experiments supported this: transcranial stimulation shifted each component independently, focal ablation of remote tissue didn't change coupling, and coupling emerged during seizures, which alter local E/I balance.
caveats: Preprint; epilepsy-patient recordings, and the seizure test is a strong perturbation rather than a graded one.

title: The Human Neocortical Neurosolver gets a human-tuned cortical column with dendritic spikes
summary: HNN's canonical neocortical circuit (pyramidal cells and interneurons in L2/3 and L5) was originally built from rodent and non-human primate data. This update tunes electrophysiological properties and synaptic connections to human tissue recordings, and adds dendritic Ca2+ spikes in L5 extratelencephalic-projecting neurons and shorter dendritic spikes in L2/3 pyramidal cells. The authors show how the model can separate somatic, synaptic and dendritic contributions to E/MEG signatures, and ship workflows and tutorials for simulating event-related responses and oscillations and recording membrane potentials, Ca2+ dynamics and synaptic currents.
caveats: Preprint; a model update, so its value depends on validation against your kind of data.

title: A whole-brain model with several receptor maps at once (Frontiers Comput Neurosci, 4 Nov).
summary: Monge-Asensio, … Kringelbach & Deco. Pharmacological resting fMRI under atomoxetine plus a whole-brain model carrying adrenergic and dopaminergic receptor maps. Atomoxetine stabilised FC dynamics within a posterior catecholaminergic network; individual receptor parameters didn't differ, but their collective weighting converged towards empirical binding affinities. A template for multi-receptor models of drugs that hit more than 5-HT2A (LSD, for instance).

title: Entropy in glucose, not just BOLD (preprint, 3 Nov).
summary: Deery, … Egan & Jamadar (Monash). Functional [18F]FDG-PET with simultaneous fMRI in 84 adults: metabolic multiscale entropy went with network metastability, cortical thickness, CMRglc and CBF, and was lower in older adults; cognition links were largely explained by age. A metabolic angle on the entropic-brain measures you use.

title: In opioid use disorder, blunted responses to aversive cues stood out more than drug-cue reactivity
venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging
summary: People with OUD (n = 64) and controls (n = 35) viewed negative, neutral and drug cues during fMRI and rated valence, arousal, stress and urge; OUD participants were followed for three months (29 abstinent, 35 relapsed). OUD participants reported more arousal, stress and urge to drug cues, but showed lower nucleus accumbens, insula and ACC responses to negative cues; whole-brain analyses also found blunted inferior frontal and precentral responses to negative cues and blunted orbitofrontal responses to drug cues. Abstinent and relapsed subgroups didn't differ on ratings or brain responses.
caveats: The relapse comparison is small and null; the authors call for replication with samples powered for longitudinal outcomes.
venue_clean: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging

title: Alcohol cues, skin conductance and the pgACC, by sex (Addiction Biology, 3 Nov).
summary: Chen, … Li (Yale). 94 adult drinkers, fMRI with skin conductance during alcohol vs neutral cues. Females had larger cue SCRs, but SCR tracked AUDIT scores only in males, as did a pgACC cluster whose cue response correlated with SCR. A small example of adding a peripheral arousal channel to cue reactivity, close to your brain–body set-up.

title: Embodied DCM: one generative model from cortex through brainstem to the sinoatrial node
summary: The authors extend dynamic causal modelling to the brain–body axis. Their Brainstem Cardiac Network is a closed-loop neural mass model of five brainstem nuclei, a viscerosensory thalamic relay and sinoatrial node dynamics, so directed effective connectivity can be estimated across the cortical–brainstem–cardiac hierarchy. As an illustrative case study, they jointly inverted simultaneous EEG and ECG from an auditory Go/No-Go task with a multimodal observation model, and showed the framework can arbitrate between competing hypotheses about cortical cytoarchitecture (granular vs agranular microcircuits).
caveats: Preprint and a methods/framework paper: the case study is illustrative, not a validation across many participants. Brainstem nuclei are latent states inferred through the model, not measured.

title: Analysing EEG by breath phase rather than clock time reveals odour responses that time-locking hides
summary: Simultaneous nasal respiration and EEG in 17 participants, with naturalistic odours (peppermint, oregano, grapefruit) delivered in sync with each person's breathing. Odours evoked respiratory phase-locked event-related spectral perturbations in frontal and temporal regions during the first breath after onset: theta during inhalation and alpha during exhalation were most discriminative, patterns obscured in standard time-locked analyses because breath duration varies. Leave-one-subject-out classification detected odours above chance (AUC 0.79 peppermint, 0.67 oregano, 0.62 grapefruit).
caveats: Small sample (n = 17) and an olfactory task; modest AUCs for two of three odours.

title: Directional brain–heart interaction with permutation conditional MI (Frontiers Netw Physiol, 6 Nov).
summary: Saibene, … Puthusserypady (DTU). Validated on synthetic coupled series, then applied to EEG + ECG in 36 people: brain–heart interaction complexity rose during mental arithmetic vs baseline, over anterior and posterior regions and both vagal and sympathovagal HRV components. See this week's explainer.

title: HRV biofeedback through a spectral DCM lens (Appl Psychophysiol Biofeedback, 3 Nov).
summary: Ma, … Moeller. Secondary analysis of an open dataset: 8 weeks of HRV biofeedback (n = 15) vs a video-game control (n = 17), resting fMRI with spectral DCM and PEB. Biofeedback increased mPFC→ACC and mPFC→thalamus effective connectivity and reduced right hippocampus→VLPFC, the latter linked to SDNN change. Small groups, but a worked example of DCM-PEB on a breathing intervention.

title: DOI makes the mouse cortex less modular, via thalamo-cortical and long-range cortical influence
summary: Widefield calcium imaging in awake mice: the psychedelic DOI, in a 5-HT2A-dependent way, acutely reduced cortical network modularity by increasing correlations between anterolateral and posteromedial cortical domains. Functional influence measurements showed increased thalamo-cortical and long-range cortico-cortical influence onto the anterolateral domain, which the authors speculate drives the increased coupling.
caveats: Mouse, one drug (DOI), acute only; the causal link from influence to coupling is described as speculation. eLife reviewed preprints carry an editorial assessment rather than an accept/reject decision.

title: Psilocybin and nucleus accumbens inhibition via astrocytes (Exp Mol Med, 5 Nov).
summary: Kang, … Koo. In rodents, psilocybin-like tryptamines raised NAc activity while lowering extracellular GABA; psilocin reduced tonic (not miniature) GABA currents in medium spiny neurons; psilocybin lowered astrocytic GABA and raised astrocytic NFATc4/ALDH5A1, with 5-HT2A antagonism blunting astrocyte calcium responses. Mesolimbic tone is relevant to the reward circuitry in your addiction work.

title: Five labs, one protocol: psilocybin's acute effects in mice replicate, most 24-hour 'antidepressant-like' effects don't
summary: Five independent laboratories ran the same experiments on psilocybin (2 mg/kg i.p.), using about 200 male and female mice per experiment. Psilocybin robustly and replicably increased anxiety- and avoidance-related behaviour and decreased fear expression acutely. But at 24 hours it did not replicably reduce anxiety- or depression-like behaviour or facilitate fear extinction, and it didn't alter social preference or social reward learning. The authors conclude that some reported persistent effects in mice may be modest and/or inconsistent.
caveats: One dose and route, and a specific behavioural battery; null replication of behaviour doesn't speak directly to structural plasticity or to human efficacy.

title: Does Gi signalling separate hallucinogenic from non-hallucinogenic 5-HT2A agonists? Two papers disagree.
summary: Miranda-Azpiazu, … González-Maeso & Meana (Neurochem Int, 6 Nov), in post-mortem human prefrontal cortex: DOI, TCB-2 and LSD activated Gq/11 and Gi1 via 5-HT2A, while non-hallucinogenic Ariadne, 2-Br-LSD and lisuride activated Gq/11 but not Gi1; they note a larger drug panel is needed. In the other corner (ICYMI, ACS Chem Neurosci, 17 Oct), Hatzipantelis & Olson reanalysed source data from an earlier Gi paper by Xu et al. and argue Gi activation is less predictive of hallucinogenic potential than canonical 5-HT2A effectors. Unresolved, and relevant to how non-hallucinogenic 'psychoplastogens' are defined.

title: doi:10.1021/acschemneuro.6c00743 (Does Gi signalling separate hallucinogenic from non-hallucinogenic 5-HT2A agonists? Two papers disagree.)
summary: Miranda-Azpiazu, … González-Maeso & Meana (Neurochem Int, 6 Nov), in post-mortem human prefrontal cortex: DOI, TCB-2 and LSD activated Gq/11 and Gi1 via 5-HT2A, while non-hallucinogenic Ariadne, 2-Br-LSD and lisuride activated Gq/11 but not Gi1; they note a larger drug panel is needed. In the other corner (ICYMI, ACS Chem Neurosci, 17 Oct), Hatzipantelis & Olson reanalysed source data from an earlier Gi paper by Xu et al. and argue Gi activation is less predictive of hallucinogenic potential than canonical 5-HT2A effectors. Unresolved, and relevant to how non-hallucinogenic 'psychoplastogens' are defined.

title: Meditative 'cessation' at 7T: consciousness switched off without global suppression (Imaging Neuroscience, 5 Nov).
summary: Yang, … Sacchet (MGH). A dense-sampling case study (N = 3) of extended cessation, a voluntary absence of reportable experience: increased activity in unimodal sensory cortices and viscerosensory brainstem nuclei, reduced activity in transmodal regions, subcortex and brainstem, with connectivity changes covarying with histamine H3 receptor maps. Tiny N, but an endogenous altered state with neuroimaging.

title: EigenBrain: which receptor maps can be approximated from MRI eigenmodes (preprint, 2 Nov).
summary: Wan, … Valk & Kirschner, with Margulies and Hansen among the authors. Of 23 molecular maps, eight (serotonin, dopamine, histamine, cholinergic and opioid markers) could be approximated from functional, but not structural or geometric, eigenmodes, then applied to autism and schizophrenia cohorts. Relevant to receptor-informed analyses of psychedelic fMRI, and to spatial autocorrelation (see Catch-up).

title: Usona has filed its psilocybin NDA for major depressive disorder (reported 2 Nov).
summary: Psychedelic Alpha reports this makes it the second psychedelic NDA under FDA review (after Resilient's MDMA refiling). Usona, like Compass, holds a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher; Compass had guided an imminent TRD filing.

title: New on ClinicalTrials.gov: psilocybin for amblyopia, targeting critical periods (first posted 5 Nov).
summary: NCT07920081, Johns Hopkins, phase 1/2, 24 planned, psilocybin doses from 1 to 25 mg combined with amblyopia therapy. A human test of the psychedelics-reopen-critical-periods idea.

title: Also new: ayahuasca vs esketamine on experimental pain (posted 2 Nov), and psilocybin for fear of cancer recurrence (posted 2 Nov).
summary: NCT07910838 (University of São Paulo, early phase 1, 20 enrolled); NCT07909408 (NYU Langone, phase 2, 100 planned, 25 mg vs 5 mg).

title: NCT07909408 (Also new: ayahuasca vs esketamine on experimental pain (posted 2 Nov), and psilocybin for fear of cancer recurrence (posted 2 Nov).)
summary: NCT07910838 (University of São Paulo, early phase 1, 20 enrolled); NCT07909408 (NYU Langone, phase 2, 100 planned, 25 mg vs 5 mg).

title: A multilevel E/I framework for how psychedelics change affect and the self
summary: A theoretical article proposing that 5-HT2A-driven shifts in excitation–inhibition balance propagate across a four-level hierarchy (homeostatic–autonomic, limbic, salience network, cortical self-referential), with post-acute plasticity and 'inhibitory recalibration' stabilising altered affective dynamics.
caveats: Single-author narrative synthesis, not a systematic review; the framework is offered as testable, but the evidence is organised narratively.

title: The clinical pharmacology of mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT) for treatment-resistant depression
summary: A narrative review built on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov and grey literature to 15 Aug 2026, plus regulatory and sponsor disclosures. It covers mebufotenin's atypical pharmacology: a non-selective serotonin agonist with high 5-HT1A affinity (Ki 3.0 nM) and markedly lower 5-HT2A affinity, with reported selectivity of roughly 30- to 300-fold depending on the assay.
caveats: Narrative rather than systematic synthesis; several authors are affiliated with the Centre for Human Drug Research (Leiden), so check their declared interests.

title: Also: Nature's consciousness spotlight (4 Nov).
summary: A journalistic overview (Heidt) of where consciousness science stands, from PCI to the adversarial GNWT vs IIT collaboration. Light reading.

title: Cortical travelling waves: mechanisms and computational principles
summary: The review that pulled together evidence for travelling waves at mesoscopic (single-area) and macroscopic (whole-brain) scales, and placed it within theory of how recurrent networks generate and propagate waves. It argues waves transiently modulate spiking and excitability as they pass and may serve functions from memory consolidation in sleep to processing dynamic visual input in the awake cortex. Why it mattered: it gave the field a shared vocabulary and a mechanistic framing (waves as a computational feature, not just a phase artefact), which much of the later EEG/MEG travelling-wave literature builds on.
caveats: A review, mostly built on invasive animal recordings; it says less about how to measure waves robustly at the scalp.
since_then: Davis, Muller et al. (Nature, 2020) showed spontaneous travelling waves in awake marmoset visual cortex predicted target detection, moving waves from anaesthesia into behaving perception. doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2802-y

title: Where does EEG come from and what does it mean?
summary: A short, provocative opinion piece arguing that we know 'shockingly little' about where EEG signals come from and what they mean. It sets out what is known, why the answers matter, and how modern circuit tools (measuring and manipulating neurons with high spatiotemporal precision) might finally provide answers, proposing oscillations as the best anchor because they're seen across scales and species. Why it mattered: it became a widely cited framing for the generators problem and a call to link scalp EEG to circuit mechanisms.
caveats: An opinion piece, not new data; much of the cross-scale work it called for has appeared since.
since_then: The Human Neocortical Neurosolver (Neymotin et al., eLife 2020) turned a laminar circuit model of EEG/MEG generators into open software; this week's preprint updates it with a human-tuned circuit. doi:10.7554/eLife.51214
code_data: Not for this paper, but HNN is open: hnn-core

title: Stomach–brain synchrony reveals a delayed-connectivity resting-state network
summary: Using simultaneous resting fMRI and electrogastrography, the authors found a 'gastric network': brain regions phase-synchronised with the stomach's slow (~0.05 Hz) electrical rhythm. It cuts across classical resting-state networks, partly overlaps autonomic regions, and is dominated by areas that map bodily and external space (somatomotor cortices through to the extrastriate body area and dorsal precuneus), with a precise temporal sequence within each gastric cycle. Why it mattered: it showed that resting-state organisation isn't only about instantaneous connectivity, and put the stomach on the map as a driver of slow brain dynamics.
caveats: Healthy participants only; EGG is noisy, and the phase-locking approach needs careful surrogate statistics.
since_then: Wolpert, Rebollo & Tallon-Baudry (Psychophysiology, 2020) published a practical EGG recording and analysis pipeline with MATLAB code and normative data from 117 people. doi:10.1111/psyp.13599

title: Neural substrates of cue reactivity and craving in gambling disorder
summary: Participants with gambling disorder in treatment (n = 19) and 19 controls viewed personally tailored gambling cues, neutral cues and appetitive food images during fMRI. Craving rose after gambling cues in the gambling group, who also showed greater insula and anterior cingulate reactivity to gambling cues but no group difference for food cues. Within the gambling group, craving correlated positively with gambling-cue activity in bilateral insula and ventral striatum, and negatively with ventral striatum–medial prefrontal connectivity.
caveats: Small groups (19 vs 19), treatment-seeking sample; personally tailored cues improve validity but complicate standardisation.
since_then: Starcke et al. (J Behav Addict, 2018) meta-analysed 18 cue-reactivity studies in gambling, gaming and buying disorders, finding higher subjective (d = 0.84) and physiological/EEG (d = 0.61) cue reactivity in patients. doi:10.1556/2006.7.2018.39

title: Generative modelling of brain maps with spatial autocorrelation (BrainSMASH)
summary: Spatial autocorrelation (SA) violates the independence assumption behind standard tests when you correlate two brain maps. The authors introduced a generative null model, released as open software, that produces surrogate maps with SA matched to a target map, for cortical, subcortical, parcellated and dense data, and showed how SA inflates p-values in map-to-map comparisons. Why it mattered: alongside spin tests, it became one of the standard ways to test map correspondences honestly, including in gene-enrichment analyses.
caveats: Results still depend on the variogram fit and parcellation; different null models can disagree.
since_then: Markello & Mišić (NeuroImage, 2021) benchmarked spatial null models, and neuromaps (Nature Methods, 2022) packaged them with a library of brain maps. doi:10.1016/j.neuroimage.2021.118052 · doi:10.1038/s41592-022-01625-w
